title: Microsoft November hotpatches can stop some apps from starting, heise reports
summary: heise reports that Microsoft's November Patchday hotpatches, deployed via Windows Autopatch to Windows 11 24H2 or newer, can stop some apps from starting with error 0xC0000099. Apps loading the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL are mainly affected; systems on standard updates are not. heise advises against uninstalling the patch because it fixes exploited vulnerabilities, and describes a registry workaround.
plain: A Microsoft November hotpatch can stop some apps from starting on Windows 11 machines updated through Autopatch, heise reports. Uninstalling it is not advised.
exec: Hotpatched Windows 11 fleets may see apps fail to start, per heise.
action: Do not uninstall the patch. heise describes setting the HotPatchTableSize registry value to 2000 (hex) after a registry backup, then restarting.

sources.name: heise online: Microsoft Hotpatching: Patchday-Flicken legen Apps lahm

date_note: Dated by heise's article; its exact date was not shown in the text read. Microsoft's own notice not read.

validation.note: Only heise read; heise cites Microsoft admin-center item WI1559710 via BleepingComputer, not read.
